manifest.name: Pi Agent Documentation Index
manifest.description: Topic index of 33 markdown and JSON documentation files across the Pi agent monorepo (ai, agent-core, coding-agent, tui packages). Tracks doc_type, status, audience, and key topics to enable AI agents to answer "which doc should I read?" for contributors, users, and operators.

analyzers.name: Docs
analyzers.description: Generates document-level topic indexing for technical docs, optimized for 'which doc should I read?' retrieval.

fields.name: file_path
fields.description: The full path to the document.

fields.name: chat_id
fields.description: The unique identifier for the file in the current chat context.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The H1 heading of the document.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: 1-2 sentence description of what this doc covers.

fields.name: topics
fields.description: Distinctive topics for retrieval. 3-18 terms, following the density table.

fields.name: section_anchors
fields.description: H2 section anchors using GitHub-style slug format for navigation.

fields.name: related_docs
fields.description: Explicit Markdown-linked documents only; normalize to repository-relative paths when possible.

fields.F4: Covers pi's compaction and branch summarization systems for managing limited LLM context windows, including auto-compaction triggers, split-turn handling, cut-point rules, the structured summary format, and extension interception events.
fields.F11: ["Split turns use two-pass summary merging (history summary + turn prefix summary).","Cut points never land at tool results—they must stay with their tool call.","File tracking accumulates cumulatively across multiple compactions and nested branch summaries."]

fields.F4: Describes three containerization patterns for isolating pi: Gondolin (local Linux micro-VM), plain Docker (whole pi process in a container), and OpenShell (policy-controlled sandbox with optional remote inference routing).
fields.F11: ["Three isolation patterns serve different needs: Gondolin for local micro-VM isolation with host auth, Docker for simplest local container boundary, OpenShell for policy-controlled sandbox.","Extensions run wherever the pi process runs—tool-routing extensions only isolate built-in tools and ! commands, not other extension tools."]

fields.F4: Reference and guide for registering custom model providers via pi.registerProvider(), covering provider overrides, new provider registration, OAuth/SSO integration, custom streaming APIs, context overflow normalization, and full config type references.
fields.F11: ["When models is provided to registerProvider, it replaces all existing models for that provider.","OAuth credentials persist in ~/.pi/agent/auth.json.","Context overflow detection uses a message_end handler to normalize error messages to context_length_exceeded prefix, enabling automatic compaction-and-retry recovery.","apiKey and header values use the same config value syntax as models.json (!command, $ENV_VAR, $$, $!)."]

fields.F4: Developer setup and contribution guide for the Pi coding agent monorepo, covering cloning, building, debugging, testing, and the project directory structure.
fields.F11: ["Use `src/config.ts` for all package asset resolution instead of `__dirname` directly."]

fields.F4: This JSON file defines the navigation structure and redirects for the Pi coding agent documentation site, organizing pages into logical sections.

Comprehensive reference for writing Pi TypeScript extensions, covering lifecycle events, custom tools, user interaction, custom UI components, commands, state management, session management, and provider registration.
fields.F11: ["Extensions auto-discover from trusted locations (`~/.pi/agent/extensions/`, `.pi/extensions/`). Built-in tool override is supported but warns. `prepareArguments` allows backward-compatible schema evolution without polluting current schema."]

fields.F4: Master index for Pi documentation, providing the navigation hub to all guides including quickstart, usage, security, customization, programmatic SDK, and platform setup topics.
Reference documentation for pi's JSON Event Stream mode, covering event types, message types, and output format for programmatic integration with pi's coding agent.
Complete reference for pi's keyboard shortcuts and customization system, covering editor controls, session management, model selection, tree navigation, and Emacs/Vim configuration examples.

Comprehensive reference for configuring custom AI providers and models in pi, covering Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio, OpenAI-compatible APIs, Anthropic Messages compatibility, OpenRouter routing, Vercel AI Gateway, and model override mechanisms.
fields.F11: ["Shell command values resolved at request time without built-in TTL or recovery logic"]

fields.F4: This documentation explains how to create, install, manage, and filter Pi packages, which bundle extensions, skills, prompt templates, and themes for sharing via npm or git.
This documentation describes Pi prompt templates, which are Markdown snippets that expand into full prompts. It covers template locations, format, usage, argument handling, and loading rules.
This documentation details the various AI providers supported by Pi, including subscription-based providers (OAuth) and API key providers (environment variables or auth file).
Entry-point tutorial for pi covering installation, authentication, first session setup, project instructions, and common operations.
Comprehensive reference for pi's RPC mode covering the JSONL protocol, all commands, event streaming, extension UI sub-protocol, error handling, and TypeScript types.
fields.F11: ["Use strict JSONL semantics with LF as only record delimiter","preflightResult callback semantics for prompt acceptance vs post-acceptance failures","BashExecutionMessage included in context only on next prompt not immediately","Extension UI uses request/response sub-protocol with dialog methods blocking until response and fire-and-forget methods not requiring response"]

fields.F4: Complete SDK reference for programmatic use of pi's agent capabilities, covering session creation, custom tools, extensions, skills, session management, settings, and run modes.
fields.F11: ["Event subscriptions are attached to a specific AgentSession and must be re-subscribed after session replacement","Settings load from global then project with project overriding global","DefaultResourceLoader discovers extensions, skills, prompts, and themes from standard directories"]

fields.F4: Security documentation for Pi coding agent, explaining that Pi operates within the local user's trust boundary without a built-in sandbox. Covers project trust controls, trust decision persistence, and guidance for running untrusted work in isolated environments.
fields.F11: ["Pi intentionally has no built-in sandbox","Isolation must come from OS or virtualization boundaries","Project trust only guards input loading, not runtime execution","Prompt injection from untrusted content is accepted local-agent risk"]

fields.F4: Comprehensive reference for Pi's session file format, covering JSONL structure, tree-based entry linking, all message and entry types, context building logic, and the complete SessionManager API for programmatic session manipulation.
fields.F11: ["Sessions use JSONL with tree structure via id/parentId for in-place branching","Version field enables automatic migration","BranchSummaryEntry preserves context from abandoned branches","CustomMessageEntry participates in LLM context while CustomEntry does not"]

fields.F4: User-facing overview of Pi's session system, covering session storage location, CLI options for resuming/naming/forking sessions, interactive commands, and the tree-based branching model for exploring alternatives.
fields.F11: ["Sessions auto-save to ~/.pi/agent/sessions/ organized by working directory","Tree structure enables in-place branching without new files","Session picker supports search, sort, named filters, rename, and delete"]

fields.F4: Comprehensive reference for all Pi agent configuration options, covering global and project-level JSON settings for model selection, thinking levels, retry behavior, compaction, networking, UI display, resources, and project trust management.
fields.F11: ["Project settings merge with global settings using shallow object merge","Trust prompts only occur in interactive mode"]

fields.F4: Brief guide explaining why shell aliases don't work in Pi's non-interactive bash mode and how to enable them by configuring shellCommandPrefix in settings.

Reference and tutorial documentation for Pi's skill system, covering skill discovery from multiple locations, on-demand loading via progressive disclosure, the Agent Skills specification compliance, frontmatter validation, and skill command registration.
fields.F11: ["Pi allows skill name to differ from parent directory despite the Agent Skills standard requiring a match","Description is required while name matching is lenient"]
fields.F12: ["allowed-tools is experimental and subject to change"]

fields.F4: Setup guide for terminal emulator compatibility with Pi's keyboard protocol handling, covering modifier key detection, escape sequences, and application-specific configurations across multiple terminal emulators.
fields.F11: ["Pi uses Kitty keyboard protocol for reliable modifier key detection","Local macOS modifier fallback used for Apple Terminal"]

fields.F4: Setup guide for running Pi on Android via Termux, covering installation prerequisites, Termux:API clipboard integration, AGENTS.md configuration, storage access permissions, and troubleshooting common issues.

Reference and tutorial documentation for Pi's theme system, covering the 51 required color tokens, theme file format, color variables, 256-color palette support, syntax highlighting colors, and HTML export configuration.
fields.F11: ["Theme loading order defined (built-in → global → project → packages → settings → CLI)","Hot-reload implemented for custom themes"]

fields.F4: Configuration guide for tmux extended key reporting to ensure Pi correctly receives modified key combinations like Shift+Enter and Ctrl+Enter.
fields.F11: ["Use extended-keys-format csi-u as recommended tmux configuration for reliable modified key forwarding."]

fields.F4: Comprehensive guide to Pi's TUI component system for building custom interactive user interfaces in extensions and custom tools, including built-in components, theming, overlays, and keyboard input.
fields.F11: ["Components must not exceed render width","Styles must be reapplied per line","Use existing components (SelectList, SettingsList, BorderedLoader) before building custom","invalidate() must rebuild themed content"]

fields.F4: Day-to-day usage reference for Pi covering interactive mode, slash commands, message queue, sessions, context files, CLI options, and design principles.
fields.F11: ["Pi keeps core small; workflow behavior pushed into extensions, skills, prompt templates, and packages","No built-in MCP, sub-agents, permission popups, plan mode, to-dos, or background bash"]

fields.F4: Setup guide for running Pi on Windows, specifying required bash shell locations and custom shell path configuration.

Comprehensive design spec for AgentHarness orchestration layer covering session persistence, runtime configuration, operation phases, turn snapshots, save points, hooks, and extension mutation semantics.
fields.F11: ["session-as-durable-state","turn-snapshot-isolation","pending-write-flushing-ordering","phase-based-structural-operations","error-normalization-to-AgentHarnessError"]
fields.F12: ["final settle timing semantics","auto-compaction decision point","retry handling","before_agent_start hook scope","abort barrier semantics"]

fields.F4: Design document for semi-durable AgentHarness implementation using session as the durable append-only state tree, covering resume requirements, recovery policies, and critical failure scenarios.
fields.F11: ["session-owns-all-durable-state","runtime-deps-not-serializable","conservative-recovery-by-default","every-mutation-durable-before-resolve"]
fields.F12: ["which config entries to persist first","whether to snapshot resolved system prompts","dependency version matching requirements","provider request journaling scope","recovery message visibility","JSONL truncation support"]

fields.F4: Design specification for the AgentHarness hooks system, defining a typed event-driven architecture for extensibility with phantom-typed HookEvent/Result model and mutation semantics.
fields.F11: ["Event types carry their own result type via phantom HookResult property instead of a spec table","Harness only calls emit() and never stores handlers directly","Observers are read-only and limited to original event","Context is a plain object not rebuilt per emit","Error policy for extensions should default to continue in coding-agent"]
fields.F12: ["Error policy for hook handlers needs explicit configuration","Source metadata for extension tracing not yet designed","Some extension capabilities are registries not hooks","emit() switch can miss custom mutation events from subclasses","Observer semantics intentionally limited to original event only"]

fields.F4: Design notes for a runtime-agnostic observability abstraction using traceOperation and PiObservability interfaces to emit structured lifecycle events without depending on OpenTelemetry or Sentry.
fields.F11: ["Pi owns a runtime-agnostic observability abstraction instead of depending on OpenTelemetry directly","AsyncLocalStorage is a runtime adapter not the core abstraction","Pi emits events passively and never creates OTel/Sentry spans itself","Default payloads are safe with no prompts completions or tool-args","Subscriber errors are swallowed and never affect Pi execution"]
